discovery: Discovery of magnetic skyrmions in solids and their emergent electromagnetism

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and University of Tokyo, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological magnetism and spintronics
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are particle-like, topologically protected spin textures. Long predicted, they were first established in real materials by these nominees. Pfleiderer and coworkers identified a skyrmion lattice in the chiral magnet MnSi by neutron scattering and showed the topological Hall effect produced by its emergent magnetic field. Tokura and coworkers imaged skyrmions directly in real space with Lorentz electron microscopy, extended them to room temperature, to thin films and to insulators, and showed they can be driven by ultralow current densities. Wiesendanger resolved nanometre-scale skyrmions at interfaces with spin-polarized STM and wrote and deleted single skyrmions one at a time. Together these experiments show that the topology of real-space spin textures produces emergent electromagnetic fields that act on conduction electrons. This principle now unifies many materials and phenomena and has opened topological spintronics, a promising route to low-power memory and logic.
